cards.caption: A stone lantern on Tangletown’s ridge — working water dressed as covered old tech.
Harry Wild Jones gave the neighborhood a medieval keep; John K. Daniels gave it knights of civic water.
Eighteen-foot figures of Health keep watch at the base — infrastructure as wonder.
Eagles crown the ribs near the dome. What other signals once threaded this hill?
Built 1931–32 with Hewitt’s prestressed concrete tank. The pumps are quiet; the silhouette remains.
Earlier views of the tower still read like a piece of lost city machinery left standing in plain sight.
Landmark, neighborhood icon, unofficial beacon — still holding Tangletown’s skyline.

decks.title: Justice Page / Washburn High
decks.tagline: Where classrooms stand, older care may have stood
decks.dates: Orphan asylum era → Washburn High 1925 → Ramsey / Justice Page

cards.caption: 1929: Washburn High from the air — and in the lower right, the orphanage that Ramsey would soon replace.
cards.attribution: Joseph E. Quigley / Hennepin County Library Digital Collections (NoC-US). MPS06805.

cards.caption: C. C. Washburn’s memorial orphan asylum once claimed this ridge. Soft lore, still being gathered — not a finished decree.
cards.attribution: Working · new placeholder. Co-gather a historic asylum photograph.

cards.caption: Torn down around 1929; a junior high rose on the care-house ground. Altered footprint, living campus.
cards.attribution: Working · new placeholder for the transition layer.

cards.caption: Washburn High and its field from above — twentieth-century school architecture on older social ground.
Justice Page Middle School and Washburn High share the ridge today. Ask gently what the plats remember.
cards.attribution: Working · new placeholder. Co-gather a street-level campus photo.

decks.title: St. John's Lutheran Church
decks.tagline: A steeple on Nicollet — and a tunnel rumor
decks.dates: Neighborhood congregation north of the school ridge

cards.caption: North of Justice Page, a pinnacle on Nicollet. Stand here and the school ridge is a short walk south.
cards.attribution: Working · new placeholder. Co-gather a clear exterior photograph.

cards.caption: In the 1930s, Washburn seniors walked here for baccalaureate. Church and campus have long shared the ridge’s calendar.
cards.attribution: Working · new placeholder. Inspired by Washburn Grist mentions (HCL school publications).

cards.caption: Neighbor lore whispers of a passage under the ridge — sacred ground to school ground. Myth, utility, or memory?
cards.attribution: Working · new. Tunnel lore is oral tradition — present gently, not as archive fact.

cards.caption: The map does not prove the tunnel. It invites you to wonder what else travels under Tangletown’s tangle.
